About 2 months ago, me and my boyfriend moved into our apartment, but shortly before we actually moved in, I quit my job. Even my gen x dad, who’s a stickler for taking a lot of crap at work, to just pull up your bootstraps and get done what needs to get done, thought it was for the best I quit. Those people were insane and malicious. But anyways, I quit that job, in August. And I’m LUCKY to be starting my new job tonight, but for a while there it was feeling extremely hopeless getting even the dumbest doors closed in my face, and I had the same question, why can’t I get a job if EVERYONE SAYS THEY ARE HIRING?! And my bf is loving and supportive but I could tell he didn’t think it was JUST the job market rn preventing me from gaining new employment. Until he decided to work for a phone company he had previously, quit the one was working at, got screwed out of both jobs, and was then unemployed with me. And the he experienced first hand how insane it is to try to find a job in this market. And he’s arguably WAYYY more hireable than me. He only got a job in time to pay our bills because he’s working for this place before too, the job he’s at now. So yeah, goes to say skills and being able to “market yourself as valuable” to recruiters is soul crushing and dehumanizing but it’s honestly the only way to get employed now. Connections, and marketing.

The reason why ppl (generally speaking) think it is different this time is because all the large AI companies made quite a big deal out of the idea that - with this level of investment and progression- AI should get to or even surpass the ability of any human worker at given tasks (which basically the job). Now, you can point out as many already did before, that the disappereance of the meanil jobs and tasks will lead to the creation of new ones. BUT, there are at least two problems with this. 1. The assumption that the new job created cannot be performed better by an AI than a human worker (which is unreasonable if we assumen an AI being generally better at most tasks) 2. Whatever is this new work created it has its value and necessity in the given economic system (one can argue we already produce a lot of cheap garbage and slop) and also fullfil a person with meaning like the job he had but lost (as an example, if you were a musician but got replaced by generated slop, and now you can work as a roadworker because there is not robot for it yet, the transition might not sit well with you)
